Era II · 2026

The year is 2026.

Ten years on, the early promise has been put to the test — prospectively, in real screening programs.

Era II · 2026

2026: two prospective studies show AI screening works.

MASAI · Sweden · RCT (~105,000)
Interval cancers non-inferior (ratio 0.88)

Sensitivity 80.5% vs 73.8% at matched specificity · ~44% less reading workload.

Gommers/Lång et al., Lancet 2026;407:505–514
PRAIM · Germany · real-world (463,000)
+17.6% cancers detected

Recall non-inferior · 6.7 vs 5.7 CDR per 1,000 · 12 sites, 119 radiologists.

Eisemann et al., Nature Medicine 2025

A third is underway: PRISM — the first large randomized trial of screening AI in the United States (Transpara; $16M PCORI; 7 sites; announced Sept 2025, recruiting). Results are years away, but it tests the US single-reader workflow directly.

Era II · 2026

The averages look strong — but what counts as the truth?

The label is not in the image — it comes from follow-up and pathology. Assigning it is a cascade of judgment calls (~163,000 EMBED exams, AUC 0.91), and it sets the denominator for every downstream number.

Era II · 2026 · not only breast

Chest CT: pulmonary embolism.

An FDA-cleared model (510(k): 94.9% sens) on two years of real-world CTPA: 86.8% overall — but far lower for non-acute, small (subsegmental), left-sided, and incidental clots.

Sensitivity vs FDA 510(k) clearance. [your group], unpublished — Aidoc PE / iPE triage evaluation, 30,678 CTPA + 37,272 routine CT (2023–2025).

Era II · 2026 → Era III

We are at the brink of Era III.

Detection is proven. But the same 2026 image — and the tissue that follows it — already tells us more than "is there cancer today?"

From one screening mammogram and its biopsy: a future-risk estimate, a cardiovascular signal, and a molecular recurrence score. The shift from finding the lesion to characterizing the patient — and much of it is available now.

Era III · 2026

Era III · 2026

Breast Arterial Calcification (BAC) as a continuous measurement (mm²).

A transformer segments breast arterial calcification on the routine mammogram and quantifies its area — turning an incidental finding into a graded, quantitative risk marker.

Segmentation: SCU-Net (your group). Dapamede et al., Eur Heart J 2026;47(18):2206–2220.
Era III · 2026
BAC predicts MACE — more calcium, more risk.

~120,000 women, two sites, racially diverse. Dose-response: mild HR 1.18–1.22 · moderate 1.38–1.47 · severe 2.03–2.22.

Era III · 2026

BAC and PAD.

BAC is medial calcification (Mönckeberg's) — the pattern that dominates PAD. In 59,854 women (~8-yr follow-up), it graded the risk of vascular intervention:

2.43
Moderate BAC
aHR vs zero BAC · 95% CI 1.50–3.94
3.62
Severe BAC
aHR vs zero BAC · 95% CI 1.93–6.82
Independent within every high-risk subgroup (age <50, DM, HTN, HLD, CKD, smoking). [your group], abstract.
Era III · 2026
BAC and valvular disease.

122,011 women, dose-response by severity (any-VHD C-index ≈0.80). Severe vs none — AS 11.4, AR 3.1, MR 2.6, TR 2.3; mitral stenosis null — a negative control. 5-yr any-VHD 19.3% vs 4.6% (NNS 7).

Era III · 2026

BAC marks a body-wide calcification tendency.

Coronary (CAC), n=2,079: detectable CAC rises 38% → 67% across BAC tiers; CAC>100 up 2.5×; independent of age (OR 1.32/SD).

Cartilage (CCC), n=1,311: a non-vascular marker — high BAC ≈ +3,408 mm³ costal-cartilage calcification at the 75th pct (adj. age, DM).

Vascular + valvular + skeletal — one free mammographic finding.

[your group], RSNA 2026 abstracts (BAC–CAC; BAC–CCC).
CAC detection by BAC tier (n=2,079).
Era III · 2026

Closing the loop: the I-BAC pragmatic trial.

The gap: <7% (Emory) / 15% (Mayo) of women had the chart data to even compute a PREVENT/ASCVD score — including women with severe BAC. I-BAC (R01HL167811) is a Hybrid Type 1 pragmatic RCT across Emory + Mayo AZ (~225,000 mammograms/yr).

AIM 1
Design the notification
CFIR formative work with patients & providers.
AIM 2
Deploy & randomize
6,000 women, moderate/severe BAC, 1:1 notify vs usual care; Carebricks AI filtering.
AIM 3
Evaluate (RE-AIM)
Reach, adoption, fidelity, maintenance, harms (anxiety, low-value testing).

Primary endpoint: 6-month composite of lipid panel · preventive-med change · CAC testing. Precedent: NOTIFY-PICTURE — but BAC has no management guideline yet.

Era III · 2026

Estimating the Oncotype DX score from the H&E slide.

Orpheus (6,172 cases, 3 institutions) infers the 21-gene Recurrence Score directly from the H&E — what imaging cannot do: morphology → molecular identity. Oncotype DX itself costs ~$4,000 and takes 1–2 weeks.

0.89 vs 0.73
flags high-risk (RS>25) vs leading nomogram
0.75 vs 0.49
predicts recurrence in low-RS patients

Era III · 2026 → 2035

And we are on the verge of multimodal, multi-omics.

Everything so far is still one model, one modality — the image, or the calcium, or the tissue, read separately.

The frontier is to combine them — imaging + pathology + genomics + the clinical record — into a single model of the patient. To see where that goes, we have to leave 2026.

Era III · 2035

The year is 2035.

From here, today's models are a decade old. The real question: what happens when imaging, pathology, and omics finally converge — on one patient.
